entities.body: The assistant town clerk, a dapper little man in a shower of hail suit who walks uncertainly on bad corns and will not glance at the list. Hell open to christians they were having about their damned Irish language. O, my corns! Come upstairs for goodness’ sake till I sit down somewhere.

entities.name: Old Barlow
entities.body: The macebearer, laid up with asthma: no mace on the table, nothing in order, no quorum even.

entities.name: Hutchinson
entities.body: The lord mayor, in Llandudno while the council sits.

entities.name: Lorcan Sherlock
entities.body: Little Lorcan Sherlock, doing _locum tenens_ for him.

entities.name: The waitress
entities.body: At the D. B. C., who takes the order for two mélanges and scones and butter and cakes, and whose tray Buck Mulligan helps to unload.

entities.name: Professor Pokorny
entities.body: Of Vienna, who can find no trace of hell in ancient Irish myth — which Haines finds rather interesting, given what is on Stephen’s mind.

entities.name: Almidano Artifoni
entities.body: Stephen’s singing teacher, round mustachioed, who tells him in Italian that he had such ideas too when he was young, that the world is a brute, and that his voice would be a source of income: instead, you sacrifice yourself. He trots in vain after the Dalkey tram with a baton of rolled music held up as a signal, and his sturdy trousers are swallowed by a closing door in the last line of the episode.

entities.name: Goldsmith
entities.body: Whose knobby poll Artifoni gazes over Stephen’s shoulder at, outside Trinity.

entities.name: Mr Lewis Werner
entities.body: Whose cheerful windows on Merrion square are as far as Cashel Boyle O’Connor Fitzmaurice Tisdall Farrell walks before turning and striding back. Not the Louis Werner who is touring Molly Bloom in episode 6.

entities.name: Mrs Stoer
entities.body: One of the three women sitting in the parlour with the blind down at the Dignams’, sniffling and sipping the superior tawny sherry uncle Barney brought from Tunney’s.

entities.name: Mrs Quigley
entities.body: The second of them.

entities.name: Mrs MacDowell
entities.body: The third. Not Gerty MacDowell, who passes the viceregal cavalcade at the end of the episode carrying cork lino letters for her father.

entities.name: Stoer
entities.body: The boy whose old fellow welted hell out of him for the packets of fags with the pictures of soubrettes in them.

entities.name: Fitzsimons
entities.body: The best pucker going for strength. One puck in the wind from that fellow would knock you into the middle of next week, man.

entities.name: Jem Corbet
entities.body: The best pucker for science, before Fitzsimons knocked the stuffings out of him, dodging and all.

entities.name: Father Conroy
entities.body: To whom Paddy Dignam went to confession on Saturday night, which is why his son hopes he is in purgatory now.

entities.name: Lieutenantcolonel Heseltine
entities.body: In the first carriage with the earl and countess of Dudley.

entities.name: The honourable Mrs Paget
entities.body: In the second carriage of the viceregal cavalcade with Miss de Courcy and the honourable Gerald Ward, one of the three ladies Blazes Boylan offers the bold admiration of his eyes and the red flower between his lips.

entities.name: Miss de Courcy
entities.body: With her.

entities.name: The honourable Gerald Ward
entities.body: A. D. C. in attendance, who is agreeably surprised when Denis Breen, shifting his tomes to his left breast, salutes the second carriage — and who makes haste to reply.

entities.name: Mr Dudley White
entities.body: B. L., M. A., who does not salute the viceregal carriages, being undecided on Arran quay whether he should arrive at Phibsborough more quickly by a triple change of tram or by hailing a car or on foot through Smithfield.

entities.name: Mina Kennedy
entities.body: Gold: the barmaid of the Ormond, of 4 Lismore terrace, Drumcondra, whose head appears with Miss Douce’s above the crossblind at the start of the viceregal cavalcade in episode 10 and watches and admires it at the end. In episode 11 she reads on behind the bar through Lenehan’s fable of the fox and the stork, plugs both ears with her little fingers rather than hear about the old fogey in Boyd’s, and serves the two gentlemen with tankards. Sadly, gold no more, she twines a loose hair behind an ear. Episode 11 gives her the first name Mina.

entities.name: Lydia Douce
entities.body: Bronze, beside her at the crossblind in episode 10, and the centre of episode 11: back from her holidays at Rostrevor sunburnt and lying out on the strand all day, with a rose on her breast and a shell from the seaside on the counter. She holds the seahorn to George Lidwell’s ear, and at Lenehan’s coaxing snaps her nipped garter smackwarm against her thigh — Sonnez la cloche — for Blazes Boylan, who drinks his sloegin and goes anyway. Episode 11 gives her the first name Lydia.

entities.name: Gerty MacDowell
entities.body: Carrying the Catesby’s cork lino letters for her father who was laid up, who knew by the style it was the lord and lady lieutenant but could not see what Her Excellency had on, because the tram and Spring’s big yellow furniture van stopped in front of her.

entities.name: Her father
entities.body: Who was laid up, and for whom she is carrying the letters.

entities.name: Mr M. E. Solomons
entities.body: In the window of the Austro-Hungarian viceconsulate, at whose head Farrell stares through a fierce eyeglass across the carriages.

entities.name: King Billy
entities.body: Whose horse’s foreleg paws the air over the spot where Mrs Breen plucks her hastening husband back from under the hoofs of the outriders.

entities.name: Wolfe Tone
entities.body: Whose statue was not on the slab the five sandwichmen eel themselves around between Monypeny’s corner and it.

entities.name: Pat
entities.body: The waiter of the Ormond: bald Pat, bothered Pat, hard of hearing, who serves the two diners their liver and their steak and kidney, brings pen, ink and a pad to blot, and mitres the napkins while the singing goes on. Bloom signs to him to set the door of the bar ajar so that the song will carry, and tips him twopence going. Pat is a waiter who waits while you wait.

entities.name: The boots
entities.body: The bar-boy who bangs his tray of chattering china on the counter, asks whose beau the man at the window is, and sniffs Imperthnthn thnthnthn at Miss Douce when she threatens to report him. Most aggravating young brat, she says: if he doesn’t conduct himself she will wring his ear for him a yard long. He is eavesdropping again in the hallway when the singing ends.

entities.name: Mrs de Massey
entities.body: Who keeps the Ormond, and to whom Miss Douce threatens to complain of the boots and his impertinent insolence. She is named once and never appears.

entities.name: George Lidwell
entities.body: Solicitor, suave, who comes into the bar in the afternoon, takes the moist hand Miss Douce gives him and holds it, and asks her, when she brings him the seahorn she carried back from the seaside, what the wild waves are saying. He drinks his Guinness through The Croppy Boy, and learns that she was not lonely walking in the moonlight by the sea: she was with a gentleman friend.

entities.name: The two gentlemen with tankards
entities.body: Who drink cool stout at the bar and pass a remark about the weather while Miss Kennedy waves her Independent about looking for where the lord lieutenant is going. They clap Simon Dedalus, order two more, and one of them is sure he knows the name Dollard: that is to say, he had heard the name of. Dollard, was it? Dollard, yes.

entities.name: The shopgirl in Daly’s
entities.body: Who sells Bloom two sheets of cream vellum paper and two envelopes for his letter to Martha, dares to say twopence, and smiles on him going. Girl there civil, he thinks. Does that to all.

entities.name: The old fogey in Boyd’s
entities.body: Whom Miss Douce asked for something for her skin and got For your what? says he. Goggle eye, greasy nose and a bit of beard: the thought of being married to him, and of the night he was in the Antient Concert Rooms, sets both barmaids shrieking before Bloom has reached the bridge.

entities.name: The barber in Drago’s
entities.body: Who always looked at Bloom’s face in the glass when Bloom spoke to his face — the thing Bloom remembers when he finds he would rather see a singer than only hear him through a door.

entities.name: The chap in Keogh’s
entities.body: Who gave them the number, after Ben Dollard and Bob Cowley had searched all Holles street for the Blooms on the night of the borrowed dress suit.

entities.name: Nannetti’s father
entities.body: Who hawked plaster figures about and wheedled at doors as Bloom does, the thought that comes to Bloom going by Ceppi’s virgins with their oils bright on them. Religion pays.

entities.name: The whore of the lane
entities.body: A frowsy whore in a black straw sailor hat askew, off her beat, who comes glazily along the quay towards Bloom in the daylight. She knew Molly and had him decked; he turns into a shop window and lets her pass. Looks a fright in the day, he thinks, and then: O, well, she has to live like the rest.

entities.name: Aaron Figatner
entities.body: Whose name Bloom’s dark eye reads going along the quay. Why do I always think Figather? Gathering figs, I think.

entities.name: Prosper Loré
entities.body: Whose huguenot name comes a few doors further on in the same walk. The two names are what the street gives Bloom to think about while he carries the sweets of sin in his breast.

entities.name: Barton James
entities.body: Of number one Harmony avenue, Donnybrook: driver of hackney car number three hundred and twentyfour, set down with his address in the flat voice of a street directory in the middle of Boylan’s jingling progress across the city.

entities.name: John Plasto
entities.body: Hatter, of number one Great Brunswick street, who made the very dressy straw hat of the young gentleman riding in that car. The same maker’s name is sweated into the leather headband of Bloom’s own high grade hat.

entities.name: Joe Maas
entities.body: The tenor Richie Goulding heard sing All is lost now one night. Maas was the boy. Massboy. A lyrical tenor if you like. Never forget it. Never.

entities.name: M’Guckin
entities.body: The other tenor of Richie’s comparison, allowed his due and no more: Ah, what M’Guckin! Yes. In his way. Choirboy style.

entities.name: Walter Bapty
entities.body: The singing master who lost his voice when a husband took him by the throat. Scoundrel, said he, you’ll sing no more lovesongs. Authentic fact, in Tom Kernan’s ginhot telling of it.

entities.name: Barraclough
entities.body: The authority on voice production Richie Goulding descants on while Bloom, hardly listening, draws and plucks the elastic thong of his packet until it snaps.

entities.name: Lablache
entities.body: The bass Father Cowley names in one word when Ben Dollard comes off The Croppy Boy to be praisefed at the bar.

entities.name: Jenny Lind
entities.body: Whose soup — stock, sage, raw eggs, half a pint of cream — is what Bloom decides a singer must be abstemious enough to live on. For creamy dreamy.

entities.name: Michael Gunn
entities.body: Who gave the Blooms the box at the theatre, the night a chap in the dresscircle stared down into Molly with his operaglass for all he was worth.

entities.name: The Shah of Persia
entities.body: Who liked the tuning up best of all the music, and wiped his nose in the curtain too. Custom of his country perhaps. That’s music too.

entities.name: Little Peake
entities.body: With whom Richie Goulding was in the gods of the old Royal the night the first note came and he never forgot it. The Peake whose name Bloom reads in the deaths column in episode 6 is not shown to be the same man.

entities.name: Mickey Rooney
entities.body: Whose band employs the chap that wallops the big drum — his vocation, Bloom decides, wondering how it first struck him, sitting at home after pig’s cheek and cabbage rehearsing his band part. Pom. Pompedy.

entities.name: Lionel
entities.body: The tenor of Flotow’s Martha, whose air M’appari Simon Dedalus is at last coaxed into singing. For the length of the song the episode calls the singer Lionel, then Lionel Simon; at the top note singer and listener fuse into one word, Siopold; and when Bloom walks out up the quay he is Lionelleopold.

entities.name: Martha
entities.body: The lost one of the opera, called back by name from the saloon — Martha! Ah, Martha! Come, you lost one — while Bloom sits over his liver with a letter to his own Martha half written. Coincidence, he thinks. Still the name: Martha. How strange! Today.

entities.name: Dolores
entities.body: The queen of the eastern seas in the song Miss Douce trills while she polishes a tumbler: O, Idolores. She returns at the end of Bloom’s Spanish daydream — under a peartree alone patio this hour in old Madrid, one side in shadow, Dolores shedolores.

entities.name: Flora
entities.body: To whose lips the dewdrops pearl did hie, in the song coming from the saloon while Lenehan lisps his low whistle of decoy over the counter.

entities.name: The croppy boy
entities.body: The boy of the ballad Ben Dollard sings: last of his name and race, his father fallen at the siege of Ross and all his brothers at Gorey, who confesses to a false priest that he has cursed three times since Easter and did not pray for his mother’s rest, and who died at Geneva barrack and was laid at Passage. Bloom listens to the confession and gets up to go before the end.

entities.name: The yeoman captain
entities.body: The false priest of the ballad, who sits vested in the gloomy chamber to shrive the boy and then rustles a soldier out of his cassock. They know it all by heart, Bloom thinks. The thrill they itch for.

entities.name: The narrator
entities.body: The nameless man who tells this episode: a collector of bad and doubtful debts, chasing Geraghty for Moses Herzog’s tea and sugar, who meets Joe Hynes at Stony Batter and drinks the afternoon out in Barney Kiernan’s on Joe’s money. How are the mighty fallen, he says of his own trade. He never gives his name and nobody in the bar uses it.

entities.name: The citizen
entities.body: The huge nationalist in the corner of Barney Kiernan’s with his dog, his cruiskeen lawn and his load of papers, working for the cause: the man who made the Gaelic sports revival and got away James Stephens, champion of all Ireland at putting the sixteen pound shot. He reads out the births and deaths of the _Irish Independent_ to prove it a national disgrace, talks Ireland’s ruined trades and emptied harbours, and ends the episode throwing a biscuitbox after Bloom down Little Britain street. The modern edition capitalises him and adds a gloss, the Citizen (the nationalist); Joyce writes him lowercase throughout.

entities.name: Garryowen
entities.body: Old Giltrap’s dog, a mangy red setter that the citizen keeps beside him and feeds at the ratepayers’ expense: growls at Bloom from the moment he comes in, ate a good part of a constabulary man’s breeches in Santry, and is credited by the newspaper parody with reciting Celtic verse under the name Owen Garry. The curse of my curses, seven days every day, on you, Barney Kiernan.

entities.name: Troy
entities.body: Of the Dublin Metropolitan police, retired, who is passing the time of day with the narrator at the corner of Arbour hill in the first sentence and gives him the wrinkle about Geraghty. The modern edition spells out D. M. P. as the Dublin police.

entities.name: Moses Herzog
entities.body: Of 13 Saint Kevin’s parade, merchant: the hop-of-my-thumb who sold Geraghty five pounds of tea and three stone of sugar on weekly instalments and cannot get a penny of it. He drink me my teas. He eat me my sugars. Because he no pay me my moneys?

entities.name: Michael E. Geraghty
entities.body: Of 29 Arbour hill, gentleman: an old plumber, the most notorious bloody robber you would meet in a day’s walk, with a face all pockmarks that would hold a shower of rain. I dare him, says he, and I doubledare him to send you round here again — for trading without a licence.

entities.name: Terry
entities.body: Terence O’Ryan, the barman in Barney Kiernan’s, who pulls the pints, brings the dog its water and its biscuit tin, and lends Alf the smutty yankee pictures he borrows off Corny Kelleher. The chivalrous Terence of the parody hands forth the crystal cup of foamy ebon ale.

entities.name: Barney Kiernan
entities.body: The publican whose house the episode is drunk in — Bernard Kiernan and Co, limited, 8, 9 and 10 Little Britain street, wholesale grocers and licensed for consumption on the premises. The dog’s verse curses him by name for having no sup of water to cool its courage.

entities.name: Willy Murray
entities.body: Whom Alf Bergan says he saw in Capel street not five minutes ago with Paddy Dignam, which is the difficulty, Dignam having been buried that morning.

entities.name: H. Rumbold
entities.body: Master barber, of 7 Hunter Street, Liverpool, who writes to the High Sheriff of Dublin offering his services at five guineas: i have a special nack of putting the noose once in he can’t get out. The parody makes him the worldrenowned headsman, stepping on to the scaffold in faultless morning dress and his favourite flower.

entities.name: Joe Gann
entities.body: Whom Rumbold hanged in Bootle jail on the 12 of February 1900, in the first line of his testimonials.

entities.name: Arthur Chace
entities.body: Private, hanged in Pentonville prison for the fowl murder of Jessie Tilsit, with Rumbold assisting.

entities.name: Jessie Tilsit
entities.body: Whom he murdered.

entities.name: Billington
entities.body: The hangman Rumbold was assistant to when the awful murderer Toad Smith was executed.

entities.name: Toad Smith
entities.body: The awful murderer.

entities.name: Herr Professor Luitpold Blumenduft
entities.body: The distinguished scientist whose medical evidence explains, at enormous length, the phenomenon Alf Bergan reports of the hanged man — the parody Bloom is interrupted before he can give in his own words.

entities.name: Giltrap
entities.body: Whose dog the citizen goes round the pubs with. Gerty MacDowell’s grandpapa, though nobody here says so.

entities.name: Pisser Burke
entities.body: Who was stopping in the City Arms hotel at the same time as the Blooms and is the narrator’s source for everything discreditable in this episode: the old one with the cracked nephew, the wife in rivers of tears with Mrs O’Dowd, the card party, the headache once a month. He takes them all off chewing the fat.

entities.name: Mrs O’Dowd
entities.body: Who kept the City Arms hotel, and cried her eyes out with Mrs Bloom in the telling.

entities.name: The old one at the City Arms
entities.body: Who had a cracked loodheramaun of a nephew and a will worth getting into; Bloom played bézique with her and would not eat meat of a Friday, and took the nephew round Dublin to teach him the evils of alcohol and brought him home drunk as a boiled owl.

entities.name: The nephew
entities.body: The cracked loodheramaun himself, afterwards in Power’s the blender’s in Cope street and going home footless in a cab five nights a week.

entities.name: Martin Murphy
entities.body: The Bantry jobber, whose _Irish Independent_ the citizen reads the English births and deaths out of. How’s that for a national press?

entities.name: William Field
entities.body: M. P., of the cattle traders, who was at the City Arms meeting about the foot and mouth disease and goes over to London tonight with Nannetti to ask about it on the floor of the house.

entities.name: Dirty Dan
entities.body: The dodger off Island bridge who sold the same horses twice over to the government to fight the Boers: Blazes Boylan’s father, in the narrator’s account of how English gold got into the family. Old Whatwhat, who called about the poor and water rate.

entities.name: Jimmy Johnson
entities.body: In whose name Joe Hynes administers the oath to Alf Bergan — the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth, so help you Jimmy Johnson.

entities.name: Signior Brini
entities.body: The eyetallyano from Summerhill, papal Zouave to the Holy Father, whose picture with Smashall Sweeney’s moustaches hangs on the Breens’ wall: a cousin of Denis Breen’s old fellow, on whose account Mrs Breen carries her nose cockahoop. A nobody, two pair back and passages, at seven shillings a week.

entities.name: James Wought
entities.body: Alias Saphiro alias Spark and Spiro: the bottlenosed swindler of the Canada case, who advertised a passage to Canada for twenty bob and swindled skivvies and badhachs from the county Meath and his own kidney too. Remanded.

entities.name: Zaretsky
entities.body: The ancient Hebrew who wept in the witnessbox with his hat on him in that case, swearing by the holy Moses he was stuck for two quid.

entities.name: Master Courtenay
entities.body: Sitting in his own chamber, who gave his rede on the same afternoon in the legal parody.

entities.name: Master Justice Andrews
entities.body: Sitting without a jury in the probate court, weighing the claim of the first chargeant on the estate of the late Jacob Halliday.

entities.name: Jacob Halliday
entities.body: Vintner, deceased, whose will is propounded there — versus Livingstone, an infant, of unsound mind, and another.

entities.name: Livingstone
entities.body: An infant, of unsound mind, on the other side of the suit over Jacob Halliday's estate in the probate court.

entities.name: Norman W. Tupper
entities.body: Wealthy Chicago contractor, in the smutty yankee picture Terry borrows off Corny Kelleher: he bounces in with his peashooter just in time to be late.

entities.name: Mrs Norman W. Tupper
entities.body: The pretty but faithless wife, found in the lap of officer Taylor, and named again in the litany of who loves whom.

entities.name: Officer Taylor
entities.body: In whose lap Norman W. Tupper finds his pretty but faithless wife, and who loves her back in the litany of who loves whom.

entities.name: Jenny
entities.body: O jakers, Jenny, says Joe to the picture, how short your shirt is. The girl of the smutty print and of the song.

entities.name: Junius
entities.body: Whose identity nobody ever settled, which is J. J. O’Molloy’s answer to Ned Lambert asking who Bloom is.

entities.name: Kakachakachak
entities.body: Surnamed Forty Warts, the Alaki’s immediate predecessor in the dynasty, out of whose skull the lovingcup of usquebaugh is drunk.

entities.name: The Alaki of Abeakuta
entities.body: His Majesty the Zulu chief of the _United Irishman_ skit, presented with an illuminated bible by the great squaw Victoria, who signs his mark in the visitors’ book at Cottonopolis and dances a charming old Abeakutic wardance, swallowing several knives and forks.

entities.name: Lord Walkup of Walkup on Eggs
entities.body: Gold Stick in Waiting, who presents the Manchester cotton magnates to him; Massa Walkup in the Alaki’s reply.

entities.name: The reverend Ananias Praisegod Barebones
entities.body: British chaplain, who freely translates the dusky potentate’s happy speech.

entities.name: Casement
entities.body: Whose report on the Congo Free State J. J. O’Molloy has read and cannot name until the citizen names him. He’s an Irishman, says the citizen.

entities.name: Cuchulin
entities.body: First of the images on the citizen’s girdle: the hero of the Ulster cycle, the hound of Culann.

entities.name: Conn of hundred battles
entities.body: High king of Ireland, second on the string.

entities.name: Niall of nine hostages
entities.body: High king, third.

entities.name: Art MacMurragh
entities.body: King of Leinster, who kept the English out of his own country for thirty years.

entities.name: Shane O’Neill
entities.body: The O’Neill of Tyrone, who went to Elizabeth’s court in his own dress and came home to fight her.

entities.name: Father John Murphy
entities.body: Of Boolavogue, who led the Wexford men in ninetyeight.

entities.name: Owen Roe
entities.body: O’Neill, who beat the Scots at Benburb and died before he could use the victory.

entities.name: Patrick Sarsfield
entities.body: Earl of Lucan, who rode to Ballyneety and afterwards took the wild geese to France; named again by John Wyse Nolan over the broken treatystone of Limerick.

entities.name: Red Hugh O’Donnell
entities.body: Of Tirconnell, who escaped from Dublin castle over the Wicklow mountains.

entities.name: Red Jim MacDermott
entities.body: The Fenian informer, on the same string as the men he betrayed.

entities.name: Soggarth Eoghan O’Growney
entities.body: The priest of the Gaelic League whose Irish lessons taught the language back to Dublin.

entities.name: Michael Dwyer
entities.body: Of the Wicklow hills, who held out five years after ninetyeight.

entities.name: Francy Higgins
entities.body: The Sham Squire, who sold Lord Edward Fitzgerald — already named in episode 10, where Ned Lambert walks Kernan past the spot.

entities.name: Henry Joy M’Cracken
entities.body: Of Belfast, hanged in ninetyeight at the Cornmarket.

entities.name: Goliath
entities.body: The Philistine giant, on an Irish hero’s girdle like everybody else.

entities.name: Horace Wheatley
entities.body: The English music-hall comedian, one of the jokes in the string.

entities.name: Thomas Conneff
entities.body: The runner.

entities.name: Peg Woffington
entities.body: The Dublin actress who took London and played Sir Harry Wildair in breeches.

entities.name: Captain Moonlight
entities.body: The name signed to the land war’s night letters, as if he were a man.

entities.name: Captain Boycott
entities.body: The Mayo land agent whose name the Land League turned into a verb.

entities.name: Dante Alighieri
entities.body: On the string between Captain Boycott and Christopher Columbus.

entities.name: Christopher Columbus
entities.body: Next to him.

entities.name: S. Fursa
entities.body: The Irish saint whose visions of the other world went into Europe before Dante’s.

entities.name: S. Brendan
entities.body: The navigator, who sailed west and is claimed here as an ancestor.

entities.name: Marshal MacMahon
entities.body: Of the Irish brigade’s descent, marshal of France and president of the republic.

entities.name: Charlemagne
entities.body: On the same girdle as Marshal MacMahon, among the Irish heroes and heroines of antiquity.

entities.name: The Mother of the Maccabees
entities.body: Who watched her seven sons die rather than eat swine’s flesh.

entities.name: Benjamin Franklin
entities.body: Among the Irish heroes and heroines of antiquity.

entities.name: Napoleon Bonaparte
entities.body: And so is he.

entities.name: John L. Sullivan
entities.body: The Boston Strong Boy, last bareknuckle champion of the world, and Irish enough for the list.

entities.name: Savourneen Deelish
entities.body: The girl of the parting song, standing in the list as if she were a person of record.

entities.name: Paracelsus
entities.body: Physician and alchemist, next to Julius Caesar.

entities.name: Sir Thomas Lipton
entities.body: The tea merchant and yachtsman.

entities.name: William Tell
entities.body: With the apple.

entities.name: Michelangelo Hayes
entities.body: The Dublin caricaturist, whose christian name does the joke for him.

entities.name: The Bride of Lammermoor
entities.body: Lucy Ashton out of Scott, on the string among the living.

entities.name: Peter the Hermit
entities.body: Who preached the first crusade.

entities.name: Peter the Packer
entities.body: Lord Chief Justice O’Brien, so called for the juries he packed — the only Peter of the two the citizen means unkindly.

entities.name: Dark Rosaleen
entities.body: Ireland under her song name, in a list of persons.

entities.name: Brian Confucius
entities.body: Confucius with an Irish christian name, one of four sages the citizen’s girdle naturalises — with Patrick W. Shakespeare, Murtagh Gutenberg and Patricio Velasquez.

entities.name: Murtagh Gutenberg
entities.body: Gutenberg, likewise made Irish.

entities.name: Patricio Velasquez
entities.body: And Velázquez.

entities.name: Captain Nemo
entities.body: Out of Jules Verne, on the same string.

entities.name: Tristan
entities.body: Of Tristan and Isolde.

entities.name: Isolde
entities.body: Whose tower stands in the list of Irish scenes at 12:417 as well.

entities.name: The first Prince of Wales
entities.body: Whom Edward the First is said to have presented to the Welsh as a prince born in Wales and speaking no English.

entities.name: Dick Turpin
entities.body: The highwayman.

entities.name: Ludwig Beethoven
entities.body: So spelled on the citizen’s girdle, between Dick Turpin and the Colleen Bawn.

entities.name: The Colleen Bawn
entities.body: Eily O’Connor of Boucicault’s play, drowned in the Shannon.

entities.name: Waddler Healy
entities.body: A Dublin character of the streets, on the girdle between Beethoven and Angus the Culdee. The text does not connect him with Tim Healy of episode 7 and neither does this package.

entities.name: Angus the Culdee
entities.body: Who wrote the martyrology of the Irish saints.

entities.name: Valentine Greatrakes
entities.body: The Waterford stroker, who cured by laying on of hands.

entities.name: Arthur Wellesley
entities.body: The duke of Wellington, whose three birthplaces are counted among the Irish scenes at 12:417.

entities.name: Boss Croker
entities.body: Of Tammany Hall, born in Cork.

entities.name: Herodotus
entities.body: Between Boss Croker and Jack the Giantkiller.

entities.name: Jack the Giantkiller
entities.body: Out of the nursery tale.

entities.name: Lady Godiva
entities.body: Of Coventry.

entities.name: Balor of the Evil Eye
entities.body: The Fomorian whose one eye killed what it looked at — the only one-eyed figure named in the Cyclops episode.

entities.name: Acky Nagle
entities.body: Of the Nagle brothers’ public house in Earl street.

entities.name: Joe Nagle
entities.body: His brother, next on the string.

entities.name: Alessandro Volta
entities.body: Whose name Joyce knew from the cinema he opened in Mary street.

entities.name: Jeremiah O’Donovan Rossa
entities.body: The Fenian, whose dynamite campaign was run from New York.

entities.name: Don Philip O’Sullivan Beare
entities.body: Last on the string: the exile who wrote the Catholic history of Ireland in Spain.

entities.name: Commendatore Bacibaci Beninobenone
entities.body: The semiparalysed doyen of the Friends of the Emerald Isle, who has to be assisted to his seat by a powerful steam crane and is afterwards extricated from underneath the presidential armchair with several hundred watches in his thirtytwo pockets.

entities.name: Monsieur Pierrepaul Petitépatant
entities.body: Second of the delegation.

entities.name: The Grandjoker Vladinmire Pokethankertscheff
entities.body: Third.

entities.name: The Archjoker Leopold Rudolph von Schwanzenbad-Hodenthaler
entities.body: Fourth, and carrying Bloom’s own two christian names into the joke.

entities.name: Countess Marha Virága Kisászony Putrápesthi
entities.body: Fifth, whose second name is Virag in Hungarian dress.

entities.name: Hiram Y. Bomboost
entities.body: Sixth.

entities.name: Count Athanatos Karamelopulos
entities.body: Seventh.

entities.name: Ali Baba Backsheesh Rahat Lokum Effendi
entities.body: Eighth.
aliases: Ali Baba Backsheesh Rahat Lokum Effendi

entities.name: Señor Hidalgo Caballero Don Pecadillo y Palabras y Paternoster de la Malora de la Malaria
entities.body: Ninth, and the longest name in the delegation but one.
aliases: Don Pecadillo y Palabras y Paternoster de la Malora de la Malaria

entities.name: Hokopoko Harakiri
entities.body: Tenth.

entities.name: Hi Hung Chang
entities.body: Eleventh.

entities.name: Olaf Kobberkeddelsen
entities.body: Twelfth.

entities.name: Mynheer Trik van Trumps
entities.body: Thirteenth.

entities.name: Pan Poleaxe Paddyrisky
entities.body: Fourteenth: Paderewski with a shillelagh.

entities.name: Goosepond Prhklstr Kratchinabritchisitch
entities.body: Fifteenth.

entities.name: Borus Hupinkoff
entities.body: Sixteenth.

entities.name: Herr Hurhausdirektorpresident Hans Chuechli-Steuerli
entities.body: Seventeenth.

entities.name: Kriegfried Ueberallgemein
entities.body: Last of the delegation, and carrying the longest title in the book: nationalgymnasiummuseumsanatoriumandsuspensoriumsordinaryprivatdocentgeneralhistoryspecialprofessordoctor.

entities.name: Constable MacFadden
entities.body: The baby policeman, a readywitted ninefooter summoned by special courier from Booterstown, who settles the delegates’ brawl over the date of Saint Patrick’s birth by proposing the seventeenth of the month.

entities.name: Avvocato Pagamimi
entities.body: Beninobenone’s legal adviser, who explains that the watches in his client’s thirtytwo pockets were abstracted in the hope of bringing their owners to their senses.

entities.name: Speranza
entities.body: Lady Wilde under her pen name, whose plaintive muse wrote the melody the York street brass and reed band play over the scaffold.

entities.name: Catalani
entities.body: The soprano — called here the eunuch Catalani — whose piercingly lovely notes beglamoured our greatgreatgrandmothers.

entities.name: Rienzi
entities.body: Whose revolution is when the commendatore’s patriarchal sombrero came into the family.

entities.name: Dr Pippi
entities.body: His medical adviser in attendance, who removes the sombrero for the prayer.

entities.name: Sheila
entities.body: The hero’s betrothed, who is folded in a loving embrace on the scaffold — Sheila, my own — and is engaged to an Oxford graduate before the execution is over.

entities.name: The Oxford graduate
entities.body: Noted for his chivalry towards the fair sex, who steps forward with visiting card, bankbook and genealogical tree, solicits her hand and is accepted on the spot; the bearer of one of the most timehonoured names in Albion’s history.

entities.name: Lieutenantcolonel Tomkin-Maxwell ffrenchmullan Tomlinson
entities.body: The stern provostmarshal presiding, who had blown a considerable number of sepoys from the cannonmouth without flinching and cannot now restrain his natural emotion.

entities.name: Messrs John Round and Sons
entities.body: The worldfamous Sheffield cutlers who supply the disembowelling appliances — a firm, but the executioner’s tools are theirs by name.

entities.name: Raftery
entities.body: The blind Connacht poet, whose satirical effusions the newspaper compares Garryowen’s verse with.

entities.name: Donal MacConsidine
entities.body: The other satirist of the comparison.

entities.name: The Little Sweet Branch
entities.body: The graceful pseudonym under which a writer of lovesongs has familiarised the bookloving world.

entities.name: Mr Joseph M’Carthy Hynes
entities.body: The wellknown and highly respected worker in the cause of our old tongue who makes the eloquent appeal for the revival of the ancient Gaelic sports — Joe Hynes with a middle name, in the newspaper’s version of the argument in the bar.

entities.name: Finn MacCool
entities.body: By whom the ancient Gaelic sports were practised morning and evening, in Joseph M’Carthy Hynes’s appeal for their revival.

entities.name: Thomas Osborne Davis
entities.body: Whose evergreen verses _A nation once again_ the citizen sings at the close of the meeting.

entities.name: The very rev. William Delany
entities.body: S. J., LL. D.: first of the clergy reported present at the meeting in Little Britain street.

entities.name: The rt rev. Gerald Molloy
entities.body: D. D., second of the clergy reported present at the Gaelic sports meeting in Little Britain street.

entities.name: The rev. P. J. Kavanagh
entities.body: C. S. Sp., third of the clergy at that meeting of the clergy reported present at the Gaelic sports meeting in Little Britain street.

entities.name: The rev. T. Waters
entities.body: C. C., fourth of the clergy reported present at the Gaelic sports meeting in Little Britain street.

entities.name: The rev. John M. Ivers
entities.body: P. P., fifth of the clergy reported present at the Gaelic sports meeting in Little Britain street.

entities.name: The rev. P. J. Cleary
entities.body: O. S. F., sixth of the clergy reported present at the Gaelic sports meeting in Little Britain street.

entities.name: The rev. L. J. Hickey
entities.body: O. P., seventh of the clergy reported present at the Gaelic sports meeting in Little Britain street.

entities.name: The very rev. Fr. Nicholas
entities.body: O. S. F. C., eighth of the clergy reported present at the Gaelic sports meeting in Little Britain street.

entities.name: The very rev. B. Gorman
entities.body: O. D. C., ninth; not the Timothy canon Gorman further down the same list.

entities.name: The rev. T. Maher
entities.body: S. J., tenth of the clergy reported present at the Gaelic sports meeting in Little Britain street.

entities.name: The very rev. James Murphy
entities.body: S. J., eleventh; not the Father John Murphy of Boolavogue on the citizen’s girdle.

entities.name: The rev. John Lavery
entities.body: V. F., twelfth of the clergy reported present at the Gaelic sports meeting in Little Britain street.

entities.name: The very rev. William Doherty
entities.body: D. D., thirteenth of the clergy reported present at the Gaelic sports meeting in Little Britain street.

entities.name: The rev. Peter Fagan
entities.body: O. M., fourteenth of the clergy reported present at the Gaelic sports meeting in Little Britain street.

entities.name: The rev. T. Brangan
entities.body: O. S. A., fifteenth of the clergy reported present at the Gaelic sports meeting in Little Britain street.

entities.name: The rev. J. Flavin
entities.body: C. C., sixteenth of the clergy reported present at the Gaelic sports meeting in Little Britain street.

entities.name: The rev. M. A. Hackett
entities.body: C. C., seventeenth of the clergy reported present at the Gaelic sports meeting in Little Britain street.

entities.name: The rev. W. Hurley
entities.body: C. C., eighteenth of the clergy reported present at the Gaelic sports meeting in Little Britain street.

entities.name: The rt rev. Mgr M’Manus
entities.body: V. G., nineteenth of the clergy at the meeting of the clergy reported present at the Gaelic sports meeting in Little Britain street.

entities.name: The rev. B. R. Slattery
entities.body: O. M. I., twentieth of the clergy reported present at the Gaelic sports meeting in Little Britain street.

entities.name: The very rev. M. D. Scally
entities.body: P. P., twentyfirst of the clergy reported present at the Gaelic sports meeting in Little Britain street.

entities.name: The rev. F. T. Purcell
entities.body: O. P., twentysecond of the clergy reported present at the Gaelic sports meeting in Little Britain street.

entities.name: The very rev. Timothy canon Gorman
entities.body: P. P., twentythird; not the B. Gorman higher up the same list.

entities.name: The rev. J. Flanagan
entities.body: C. C., last of the clergy reported present at the meeting of the clergy reported present at the Gaelic sports meeting in Little Britain street.

entities.name: P. Fay
entities.body: One of the two laymen the report troubles to name.

entities.name: T. Quirke
entities.body: The other, and then etc., etc.

entities.name: Ole Pfotts Wettstein
entities.body: Bennett’s second, who threw in the towel while the Portobello bruiser was being counted out.

entities.name: The twelve tribes of Iar
entities.body: The jury of the legal parody: one man for every tribe, of the tribe of Patrick and of Hugh and of Owen and of Conn and of Oscar and of Fergus and of Finn and of Dermot and of Cormac and of Kevin and of Caolte and of Ossian, twelve good men and true, sworn by Him Who is from everlasting.

entities.name: Juvenal
entities.body: In whose time Irish wool was sold in Rome, by the citizen’s account of the trade.

entities.name: Jacquard de Lyon
entities.body: Since when we have had our Huguenot poplin.

entities.name: Tacitus
entities.body: Read Tacitus and Ptolemy, even Giraldus Cambrensis, says the citizen: his three authorities for what Ireland was.

entities.name: Ptolemy
entities.body: The second of them, whose map has Ireland on it.

entities.name: Giraldus Cambrensis
entities.body: The third, and the least friendly witness of the three.

entities.name: King Philip of Spain
entities.body: Who offered to pay customs duties for the right to fish in Irish waters.

entities.name: The earl of Desmond
entities.body: Who could make a treaty with the emperor Charles the Fifth himself.

entities.name: The emperor Charles the Fifth
entities.body: With whom he made it.

entities.name: Henry Tudor
entities.body: Whose harps the citizen will not have on the first Irish battleship.

entities.name: Milesius
entities.body: Whose three sons are the three crowns on the blue field, the oldest flag afloat.

entities.name: Sir John Beresford
entities.body: The old ruffian who called a flogging a rump and dozen, where the modern God’s Englishman calls it caning on the breech.

entities.name: Granuaile
entities.body: Grace O’Malley, whose sons went to the land of the free and remember the land of bondage.

entities.name: Ulysses Browne of Camus
entities.body: Fieldmarshal to Maria Teresa, one of the wild geese John Wyse Nolan counts up: and what did we ever get for it?

entities.name: Maria Teresa
entities.body: Whose fieldmarshal he was.

entities.name: O’Donnell, duke of Tetuan
entities.body: Another of them, in Spain.

entities.name: George the elector
entities.body: First of the sausageeating bastards on the throne, in Joe Hynes’s account of the house of Hanover.

entities.name: Old Vic
entities.body: Queen Victoria as the bar remembers her: blind drunk in her royal palace every night of God with her jorum of mountain dew, her coachman carting her up body and bones to bed while she pulls him by the whiskers and sings him bits of Ehren on the Rhine. The same queen who is a scion of the house of Brunswick on Alf Bergan’s testoon at 12:85 and the great squaw Victoria of the Alaki’s bible at 12:442.

entities.name: Edward Guelph-Wettin
entities.body: Edward the peacemaker, of whom there is a bloody sight more pox than pax, whose room in Maynooth the bishops did up in his racing colours. The earl of Dublin, no less.

entities.name: Cromwell
entities.body: Sanctimonious Cromwell and his ironsides, who put the women and children of Drogheda to the sword with the bible text God is love pasted round the mouth of his cannon.

entities.name: Solomon of Droma
entities.body: To whom, with Manus Tomaltach og MacDonogh, the Book of Ballymote is attributed, and with it the muchtreasured facecloth the citizen swabs himself dry with.

entities.name: Manus Tomaltach og MacDonogh
entities.body: The other author of the Book of Ballymote.

entities.name: Li Chi Han
entities.body: Who lovey up kissy Cha Pu Chow.

entities.name: Cha Pu Chow
entities.body: Whom he loves.

entities.name: Jumbo
entities.body: The elephant, who loves Alice the elephant.

entities.name: Alice
entities.body: The elephant he loves.

entities.name: Old Mr Verschoyle
entities.body: With the ear trumpet, who loves old Mrs Verschoyle.

entities.name: Old Mrs Verschoyle
entities.body: With the turnedin eye, who is loved by him.

entities.name: Mary Kelly
entities.body: Whom Constable 14A loves.

entities.name: Constable 14A
entities.body: Who loves her; the bobby Paddy Leonard knew the night Bob Doran was near being lagged.

entities.name: Messrs Alexander Thom’s
entities.body: Printers to His Majesty, where Lipóti Virag was lately employed, in the farewell report of his departure for the Meadow of Murmuring Waters.

entities.name: Mr George Fottrell
entities.body: The much respected clerk of the crown and peace, whose headgear was found after the earthquake on the third basaltic ridge of the giant’s causeway.

entities.name: Mercalli
entities.body: On whose scale the observatory of Dunsink registered all eleven shocks.

entities.name: The chevalier Jean Wyse de Neaulan
entities.body: Grand high chief ranger of the Irish National Foresters: John Wyse Nolan ennobled and married off to a fir tree, because he said something about reafforesting the land.

entities.name: Miss Fir Conifer
entities.body: Of Pine Valley, the bride, given away by her father the M’Conifer of the Glands in green mercerised silk with hip insertions of acorn bronze.

entities.name: The M’Conifer of the Glands
entities.body: Her father.

entities.name: Miss Larch Conifer
entities.body: One of the two maids of honour, sisters of the bride.

entities.name: Miss Spruce Conifer
entities.body: The other.

entities.name: Lady Sylvester Elmshade
entities.body: First of the guests who graced the ceremony by their presence.

entities.name: Mrs Barbara Lovebirch
entities.body: Second. Not James Lovebirch of _Fair Tyrants_, whose book Molly did not like.

entities.name: Mrs Poll Ash
entities.body: Third.

entities.name: Mrs Holly Hazeleyes
entities.body: Fourth.

entities.name: Miss Daphne Bays
entities.body: Fifth, and the only guest whose name was a tree before it was a woman.

entities.name: Miss Dorothy Canebrake
entities.body: Sixth.

entities.name: Mrs Clyde Twelvetrees
entities.body: Seventh.

entities.name: Mrs Rowan Greene
entities.body: Eighth.

entities.name: Mrs Helen Vinegadding
entities.body: Ninth.

entities.name: Miss Virginia Creeper
entities.body: Tenth.

entities.name: Miss Gladys Beech
entities.body: Eleventh.

entities.name: Miss Olive Garth
entities.body: Twelfth.

entities.name: Miss Blanche Maple
entities.body: Thirteenth.

entities.name: Mrs Maud Mahogany
entities.body: Fourteenth.

entities.name: Miss Myra Myrtle
entities.body: Fifteenth.

entities.name: Miss Priscilla Elderflower
entities.body: Sixteenth.

entities.name: Miss Bee Honeysuckle
entities.body: Seventeenth.

entities.name: Miss Grace Poplar
entities.body: Eighteenth.

entities.name: Miss O Mimosa San
entities.body: Nineteenth, out of _The Geisha_ by way of the shrubbery.

entities.name: Miss Rachel Cedarfrond
entities.body: Twentieth.

entities.name: Miss Lilian Lilac
entities.body: One of the Misses Lilac.

entities.name: Miss Viola Lilac
entities.body: The other.

entities.name: Miss Timidity Aspenall
entities.body: Twentythird.

entities.name: Mrs Kitty Dewey-Mosse
entities.body: Twentyfourth.

entities.name: Miss May Hawthorne
entities.body: Twentyfifth.

entities.name: Mrs Gloriana Palme
entities.body: Twentysixth.

entities.name: Mrs Liana Forrest
entities.body: Twentyseventh.

entities.name: Mrs Arabella Blackwood
entities.body: Twentyeighth.

entities.name: Mrs Norma Holyoake
entities.body: Of Oakholme Regis, last of the guests.

entities.name: Senhor Enrique Flor
entities.body: Who presided at the organ with his wellknown ability and played _Woodman, spare that tree_ at the conclusion of the service.

entities.name: Benedict of Spoleto
entities.body: Whose monks head the procession, before the Carthusians and Camaldolesi.

entities.name: Peter Nolasco
entities.body: Whose children walk with the friars of Augustine and the Trinitarians.

entities.name: Albert bishop
entities.body: Who leads the children of Elijah prophet down from Carmel mount with Teresa of Avila.

entities.name: Teresa of Avila
entities.body: Calced and other, at the head of the Carmelites.

entities.name: Poor Francis
entities.body: Whose sons walk brown and grey: capuchins, cordeliers, minimes and observants.

entities.name: Clara
entities.body: Whose daughters walk with them.

entities.name: Dominic
entities.body: Whose sons are the friars preachers.

entities.name: Vincent
entities.body: Whose sons come after the friars preachers.

entities.name: S. Wolstan
entities.body: Whose monks come next.

entities.name: Ignatius
entities.body: And Ignatius his children.

entities.name: The reverend brother Edmund Ignatius Rice
entities.body: Who leads the confraternity of the christian brothers.

entities.name: S. Cyr
entities.body: First of all the saints and martyrs, virgins and confessors who come after.

entities.name: S. Isidore Arator
entities.body: Isidore the Ploughman.

entities.name: S. James the Less
entities.body: Third.

entities.name: S. Phocas of Sinope
entities.body: The gardener who dug his own grave for his executioners.

entities.name: S. Julian Hospitator
entities.body: Who killed his parents by mistake and kept a ferry in penance.

entities.name: S. Felix de Cantalice
entities.body: Sixth.

entities.name: S. Simon Stylites
entities.body: Who lived on a pillar.

entities.name: S. Stephen Protomartyr
entities.body: The first martyr, stoned — and not Stephen Dedalus, whose alias had to be kept off this paragraph by hand.

entities.name: S. John of God
entities.body: Whose name is also the asylum the narrator says their friend is out in, off his head, in the first page of the episode.

entities.name: S. Ferreol
entities.body: Tenth.

entities.name: S. Leugarde
entities.body: Eleventh.

entities.name: S. Theodotus
entities.body: Twelfth.

entities.name: S. Vulmar
entities.body: Thirteenth.

entities.name: S. Richard
entities.body: Fourteenth.

entities.name: S. Vincent de Paul
entities.body: Of the Lazarists and the charities that carry his name.

entities.name: S. Martin of Todi
entities.body: Sixteenth.

entities.name: S. Martin of Tours
entities.body: Who cut his cloak in two for a beggar.

entities.name: S. Alfred
entities.body: Eighteenth.

entities.name: S. Denis
entities.body: Who carried his own head to Montmartre.

entities.name: S. Cornelius
entities.body: Twentyfirst.

entities.name: S. Leopold
entities.body: Twentysecond, and Bloom’s own name among the saints.

entities.name: S. Bernard
entities.body: Twentythird.

entities.name: S. Terence
entities.body: Twentyfourth.

entities.name: S. Edward
entities.body: Twentyfifth.

entities.name: S. Owen Caniculus
entities.body: Owen the little dog: the citizen’s Garryowen canonised, or Owen Garry as the newspaper has him.

entities.name: S. Anonymous
entities.body: First of the six saints whose names are the names of having no name: Anonymous, Eponymous, Pseudonymous, Homonymous, Paronymous and Synonymous.

entities.name: S. Eponymous
entities.body: The second of them.

entities.name: S. Pseudonymous
entities.body: The third.

entities.name: S. Homonymous
entities.body: The fourth.

entities.name: S. Paronymous
entities.body: The fifth.

entities.name: S. Synonymous
entities.body: The sixth.

entities.name: S. Laurence O’Toole
entities.body: Archbishop of Dublin when the Normans came.

entities.name: S. James of Dingle and Compostella
entities.body: Whose pilgrim road ran from Kerry to Galicia.

entities.name: S. Columcille
entities.body: Of Iona, who is also S. Columba two words later in the same procession: the litany gives him both his names and walks him past twice.

entities.name: S. Celestine
entities.body: Thirtieth.

entities.name: S. Colman
entities.body: Of Cloyne, or of Lindisfarne, or one of the hundred and more Colmans in the Irish calendar.

entities.name: S. Kevin
entities.body: Of Glendalough, whose parade Moses Herzog lives on.

entities.name: S. Frigidian
entities.body: Of Lucca, an Irishman abroad.

entities.name: S. Senan
entities.body: Of Scattery island.

entities.name: S. Fachtna
entities.body: Of Ross.

entities.name: S. Gall
entities.body: Columbanus’s companion, who gave his name to a Swiss canton.

entities.name: S. Fintan
entities.body: Of Clonenagh.

entities.name: S. John Nepomuc
entities.body: Of Prague, drowned for keeping the seal of confession — which is the crime the croppy boy’s false priest broke in episode 11.

entities.name: S. Ives of Brittany
entities.body: Patron of lawyers, walking behind Thomas Aquinas.

entities.name: S. Michan
entities.body: Of the church and the crypt on whose land this whole episode takes place: in Michan’s land, bedight in sable armour, comes O’Bloom the son of Rory.

entities.name: S. Herman-Joseph
entities.body: Of Steinfeld.

entities.name: S. Aloysius Gonzaga
entities.body: First of the three patrons of holy youth.

entities.name: S. Stanislaus Kostka
entities.body: The second.

entities.name: S. John Berchmans
entities.body: The third.

entities.name: S. Gervasius
entities.body: One of the three saints Gervasius, Servasius and Bonifacius.

entities.name: S. Servasius
entities.body: The second of them.

entities.name: S. Bonifacius
entities.body: The third.

entities.name: S. Brigid
entities.body: Of Kildare, who walks this procession twice under both her names: S. Bride among the Irish saints and S. Brigid among the virgins.

entities.name: S. Kieran
entities.body: Of Clonmacnois.

entities.name: S. Jarlath of Tuam
entities.body: Whose see is in Connacht.

entities.name: S. Finbarr
entities.body: Of Cork.

entities.name: S. Pappin of Ballymun
entities.body: Of a parish on the north edge of Dublin, walking the procession with S. Finbarr of Cork.

entities.name: Brother Aloysius Pacificus
entities.body: Who walks with Brother Louis Bellicosus: peace and war in two habits.

entities.name: Brother Louis Bellicosus
entities.body: The warlike one of the pair.

entities.name: S. Rose of Lima
entities.body: One of the two saints Rose, of Lima and of Viterbo.

entities.name: S. Rose of Viterbo
entities.body: The other.

entities.name: S. Mary of Egypt
entities.body: The penitent of the desert.

entities.name: S. Lucy
entities.body: Of Syracuse, who carries her eyes on a dish among the blessed symbols. Not Lousy Lucy of episode 9, whose alias had to be kept off this paragraph.

entities.name: S. Attracta
entities.body: Of Killaraght.

entities.name: S. Dympna
entities.body: Of Gheel, patron of the mad.

entities.name: S. Ita
entities.body: Of Killeedy, foster mother of the Irish saints.

entities.name: S. Marion Calpensis
entities.body: Molly Bloom canonised under the rock of Gibraltar: Calpe is the rock, and Marion is her name. The only saint in the procession born in this book.

entities.name: The Blessed Sister Teresa of the Child Jesus
entities.body: Of Lisieux, beatified the year before the book was finished and walking here among the older saints.

entities.name: S. Barbara
entities.body: Of the tower and the lightning, between S. Teresa of the Child Jesus and S. Scholastica in the procession.

entities.name: S. Scholastica
entities.body: Benedict’s sister.

entities.name: S. Ursula
entities.body: With eleven thousand virgins, last of the blessed company. Not the Ursula out of whose room Buck Mulligan pinched the shaving mirror.

entities.name: Malachy
entities.body: Who attends Father O’Flynn with Patrick under the canopy of cloth of gold at the end of the procession: the archbishop of Armagh, not the high king Malachi of the citizen’s girdle and not Buck Mulligan, whose alias is suppressed here.

entities.name: O’Connell Fitzsimon
entities.body: A chieftain descended from chieftains, who takes toll of the herds and fatlings coming into the shining palace of the Inisfail parody: the superintendent of the Dublin cattle market.

entities.name: Bungiveagh
entities.body: One of the noble twin brothers who brew the foamy ebon ale in their divine alevats, cunning as the sons of deathless Leda: Lord Iveagh with a bung in his name.

entities.name: Bungardilaun
entities.body: The other brother, Lord Ardilaun.

entities.name: Leda
entities.body: Whose deathless sons the brewers are as cunning as.

entities.name: Black Liz
entities.body: Our hen, who lays eggs for us and is so glad when she lays her egg — and under whom good uncle Leo puts his hand and takes her fresh egg.

entities.name: Joseph Manuo
entities.body: The name Bob Doran gave himself when he was calling himself a Frenchy for the two shawls in the Bride street shebeen, talking against the Catholic religion.

entities.name: The mother
entities.body: Who kept a kip in Hardwicke street and procures rooms to street couples: the bumbailiff’s widow, mother of the little sleepwalking bitch Bob Doran married and of Jack Mooney, who made him toe the line.

entities.name: Bob Doran’s wife
entities.body: Jack Mooney’s sister, who used to be stravaging about the landings at two in the morning without a stitch on her and now wags her tail up the aisle of the chapel in patent boots and violets, nice as pie, doing the little lady.

entities.name: Mr Cowe Conacre
entities.body: Multifarnham, Nationalist: who asks the right honourable gentleman in the house of commons whether the government has ordered these animals slaughtered without medical evidence, and follows it with the Mitchelstown telegram.

entities.name: Mr Allfours
entities.body: Tamoshant, Conservative: the answer to the honourable member’s question is in the affirmative.

entities.name: Mr Orelli O’Reilly
entities.body: Montenotte, Nationalist: who asks whether similar orders have been issued for the slaughter of human animals who dare to play Irish games in the Phoenix park. The answer is in the negative.

entities.name: Mr Staylewit
entities.body: Buncombe, Independent: Don’t hesitate to shoot. (Ironical opposition cheers.)

entities.name: Cummins
entities.body: Of Francis street, in whose private office J. J. O’Molloy pawned his gold watch where no-one would know him, and where the narrator was with Pisser Burke releasing his boots out of the pop.

entities.name: Dunne
entities.body: The name J. J. O’Molloy gave at the counter. What’s your name, sir? Dunne, says he. Ay, and done, says I.

entities.name: Deadwood Dick
entities.body: Of the slouch hats in the newspaper picture, firing at a man strung up in a tree with a bonfire under him: Black Beast Burned in Omaha, Ga.

entities.name: Lanty MacHale
entities.body: Whose goat would go a piece of the road with everyone — the narrator’s figure for Bloom, who is neither one thing nor the other.

entities.name: Messrs Jacob agus Jacob
entities.body: The makers of the silver casket presented to Lipóti Virag on his departure, tastefully executed in the style of ancient Celtic ornament.

entities.name: Messrs Michael Meade and Son
entities.body: Of 159 Great Brunswick street, to whom the work of salvage and removal of human remains after the earthquake is entrusted.

entities.name: The poor old woman
entities.body: Who told us the French were on the sea and landed at Killala: Ireland herself, in the song Ned Lambert quotes against the citizen’s patience.

entities.name: Bloom the dentist
entities.body: The other Bloom of Dublin, whose dental windows Father Conmee’s eye passes in episode 10 and whom Jack Power takes for a cousin of Leopold’s in episode 12. Not at all, says Martin Cunningham. Only namesakes.
